metin_k: Put in {p:10} every day and in a month you have {p:300}. Money that waits grows; money that is spent is gone.
metin_b: Saving means holding today's wish for a bigger wish tomorrow. Small regular amounts add up more easily than one big amount.
soru: If you save {p:50} every week, how much do you have after 10 weeks?

hatirla.soru: Which gives you more money by the end of the month?

metin_k: Last year a sandwich cost {p:10}, this year it costs {p:15}. Your money stayed the same, but it buys less.
metin_b: When prices go up in general, the same money buys fewer things; this is called inflation. Assets like gold and foreign currency often rise along with it, so saving only cash is not enough.
soru: You have {p:100} and prices went up by 50%. A year later, how many sandwiches can you buy?

hatirla.soru: Ice cream cost {p:10} last year and {p:15} today. What is this called?

metin_k: Gold has been valuable for thousands of years. It doesn't jump fast, but it doesn't fall easily either.
metin_b: People turn to gold when they trust money less. It moves little in the short run and keeps its value over the long run. Pure gold is called 24 karat.

metin_k: The dollar is another country's money. Some days it goes up, some days it goes down.
metin_b: An exchange rate is how much one country's money is worth in another's. News, interest rates and trust move it. Jumps are normal; the long road is what matters.
soru: Zippy dropped one day. What do you do?

hatirla.soru: The dollar dropped a little today. What does it mean?
secenekler: Prices go up and down, waiting helps
I should spend it all now

metin_k: You don't put everything in one basket. While one is gloomy, another one smiles.
metin_b: Different assets rise at different times. Splitting your savings keeps one character's bad day from affecting the whole camp.
soru: Giving all your money to one character is…
secenekler: Risky: if it falls, everything falls

hatirla.soru: Why is it good to split your money between characters?
secenekler: If one falls, the others stay

metin_k: Last month {p:250} bought more gold. Gold got pricier, so the same money buys less.
metin_b: When an asset's price goes up, the same amount of money buys less of it, while what you already own becomes worth more. Price and quantity work in opposite directions.

hatirla.soru: You have 1 gram of gold and gold got cheaper. How many grams do you have?

metin_k: Waiting is easier when you have a goal. Know what you want and count how many feedings it takes.
metin_b: A goal gives saving a meaning. A goal with an amount and a date makes every feeding measurable: 'I'm 38% of the way to my bike'.
soru: For a {p:3000} goal, if you save {p:150} a week, how long will it take?

hatirla.soru: For a {p:100} goal, if you put in {p:25} a week, how many weeks will it take?

metin_k: Water is a need. A third toy is a want. Both are fine, but one comes first.
metin_b: Needs are a must, wants are a choice. Putting pocket money first toward needs, then savings, then wants is a healthy order.

metin_k: Sharing part of your pocket money is a choice too. Even a small share can make someone's day.
metin_b: Spend · Save · Share. Three jars teach that money is not only for us. The shared part can be small but regular.

metin_k: A campfire doesn't grow in a day. Every feeding is a small log. Look back at the end of the year and see how big it got.
metin_b: Time is the strongest force in saving. A child who starts early and feeds a little but regularly can get ahead of one who starts late and puts in a lot.
secenekler: Putting in a lot one day

hatirla.soru: What does waiting a day before buying something give you?
secenekler: I find out if I really want it
